## 4bc78768be8b

**Reproduced teaching/support defect; no audit-target fix made.** Against generator source SHA-256 `5fee237462cf0d46b5b94588f7718480d1cc244145499faf27dc603d1e846688` (version 1.1.1) and executed rule hash `b5f96aa039c4`, the rival “recolor every color-2 cell yellow” matched the public Racket output on **60/60 ordinary generated inputs** (20 per difficulty band) but matched **0/5 canonical labeled pairs**. Thus the generated distribution supports a wrong color-only shortcut that canonical examples refute.

Canonical train pair 0 is the retained exact counterexample. At zero-based cells `(1,1)`, `(1,2)`, `(2,1)`, and `(2,2)`, the authority leaves color 2 while the rival writes color 4; at `(4,4)`, the authority writes color 4 while the rival leaves color 8. The public Racket result and rival output therefore differ on five cells. This input is canonical and the 60 sampled generated cases are ordinary validator-accepted generator outputs.

Two supporting defects were also reproduced. Same-seed generation was byte-identical when changing the advertised controls `palette_kind` (`warm`/`cool`), `anchor_corner=false`, `asymmetry_force=false`, and `texture=warm`, indicating those axes were ignored in the tested path. In addition, `_draw_from_degenerate("equal_sizes")` returned a grid that `self_check` accepted with `[]`, despite lacking a unique smallest component.

Exact sample schedule, grids, hashes, domain status, ignored-control comparisons, and cell differences are in `checks/audit/4bc78768be8b/evidence.json`; the public authority record is `checks/audit/4bc78768be8b/racket.json`, and rival outputs are `checks/audit/4bc78768be8b/rival_outputs.json`. This audit reports the defect only; task `4bc78768be8b` was left unchanged as required.

## 4bc78768be8b

**Reproduced defect — the generated distribution leaks the answer through the
fixed color 2.** Current generator SHA-256 is
`5fee237462cf0d46b5b94588f7718480d1cc244145499faf27dc603d1e846688`
(version `1.1.1`; no declared `RULE_HASH`). On 60 generated inputs (20 per
difficulty band), the smallest component was always color 2, so the shortcut
“recolor every color-2 cell yellow” matched the intended smallest-object rule
on **60/60** cases. The same shortcut matched **0/5** canonical labeled pairs,
while an independent smallest-component mirror matched 5/5. Full rows, seeds,
input hashes, component sizes, and canonical comparisons are retained at
`checks/audit/4bc78768be8b/evidence.json`; the smallest canonical witness is
`checks/audit/4bc78768be8b/canonical-witness.json`.

The in-domain generated witness at seed `410000`, sample index `0`, difficulty
`easy` passes `self_check`. Its input and rival are
`checks/audit/4bc78768be8b/input.json` and
`checks/audit/4bc78768be8b/rival-output.json`. Actual selected Racket execution
(rule hash `b5f96aa039c4`) is retained at
`checks/audit/4bc78768be8b/racket.json` and exactly matches that shortcut output.
The same probe also found that advertised `palette_kind`, `anchor_corner`,
`asymmetry_force`, and `texture` controls—and even an unknown `typo_axis`—all
returned the identical baseline grid. Finally, `texture="equal_sizes"`
produces two equal 4-cell components, yet `self_check` returns no error and the
rule leaves the grid unchanged, contradicting the documented unique-smallest
invariant. This confirms the active unresolved finding already indexed for the
same source bytes; I did not modify this audit-only target.

An optional official `defect_lint` audit run was interrupted before it produced
a final receipt (`checks/audit/4bc78768be8b-defect-lint.log`), so none of the
claims above depends on that incomplete run.
